job.domain: an HR and finance helpdesk assistant

items.text:
Internal Audit Summary — Security Audit SA-2024-Q3

Scope: The audit covered access review on the finance ledger, the HRIS export pipeline, and the procurement payment run for the period 1 July to 30 September. Sample size was 45 transactions, plus a full review of all 12 privileged-account changes.

Findings:
| ID | Finding | Severity | Owner | Remediation date |
|----|---------|----------|-------|------------------|
| SA-04 | Two leavers retained HRIS read access 11 days beyond termination | High | People Ops | 15 Oct |
| SA-07 | Payment run approver and checker same individual in 3 of 45 samples | Medium | Finance Systems | 31 Oct |
| SA-11 | Export pipeline logs rotate after 7 days, below the 30-day retention policy | Low | Platform Eng | 30 Nov |

All 12 privileged-account changes held a valid ticket reference and a second approver. No anomalies were identified in the payroll reconciliation during the sample period.

The audit team has asked People Ops to confirm the leaver-access fix in writing by the remediation date. Finance Systems will re-run the four-eyes check on the payment workflow before the next month-end close. A follow-up review is scheduled for the week of 4 December.
Finance Systems confirmed the new four-eyes setting on the payment run goes live Monday; the helpdesk chatbot entry in the knowledge base has been updated to reflect the change.

The holiday rota for the finance shared-services desk has been drafted for the Christmas period and is attached to this note. Priority cover is in place for payroll cut-off (18-20 December) and the bank holiday closure days. Two colleagues in the accounts-payable team have requested a swap; both managers have approved in principle, and the rota will be republished once the changes are confirmed. The overnight invoice chatbot will continue to run unattended through the closure, with escalation to the on-call analyst for anything it cannot classify. Anyone who cannot see their shift should raise a ticket with the rota coordinator before Friday.
Recall notice RCA-2024-118 applies to the batch of desk chargers with serial prefixes beginning XD7B; Finance has been asked to flag any expense claims referencing affected units.

Meeting notes — Product Recall Working Group

Date: 9 October, 10:00-10:45. Present: R. Okafor (chair, Customer Ops), L. Fenwick (Finance), S. Dhaliwal (People Ops), M. Trent (Legal).

1. Status. Recall RCA-2024-118 covers 3,400 units. Customer Ops has mailed 2,910 affected customers; the remaining 490 are next-of-kin or business accounts and are being handled by phone. Legal confirmed the wording of the public notice is cleared.
2. Finance. Reimbursement of affected expense claims is being processed in a single batch on Friday. L. Fenwick noted refunds under £50 will be paid directly and anything above that needs a manager sign-off. A question was raised about whether the automated triage tool that sorts incoming claims can be taught to recognise the affected serial prefix; L. Fenwick will check with Procurement whether the supplier can supply a clean serial list. Deferred to next meeting.
3. People Ops. No staff injury reported. S. Dhaliwal will confirm the replacement stock delivery window with the supplier and circulate the tracked-post guidance for returned units.
4. Actions. (a) Trent to file the notice copy — done. (b) Okafor to share the call-script log — due 14 Oct. (c) Fenwick to confirm the serial list — due 16 Oct.

Next meeting: 23 October, same time.
The rota coordinator flagged that the draft holiday rota for the records team still shows J. Patel on the Boxing Day shift; that should be M. Aldridge.

Policy extract — Expense Claims During a Product Recall

Where a supplier issues a recall affecting equipment that employees have purchased on company expense, the following applies. Affected claims should be flagged at submission with the recall reference (for example RCA-2024-118) in the notes field. Claims under £50 are reimbursed directly; claims above that threshold require line-manager approval before payment. Employees must not return recalled units at their own expense; a prepaid label will be issued by the supplier and tracked post must be used.

The finance helpdesk operates an automated assistant that answers common questions about claim status and thresholds. It draws on the current version of this policy, so the policy owner must keep it up to date; outdated thresholds in the knowledge base are the most frequent source of incorrect answers. The assistant cannot approve claims and will always direct anything over the threshold to a manager.

Recall-related claims are batched and paid on the Friday following approval. Any employee who has not received a refund within ten working days of approval should raise a ticket with the finance helpdesk quoting the original claim number. Disputes about whether a device is in scope are handled by Procurement, not Finance.
Security audit fieldwork is complete; the only significant finding was delayed removal of access for leavers, and the closing meeting is set for 21 November.
Reminder: the holiday rota is a shared document — please do not overwrite the tabs reserved for the records and payroll teams.

The finance helpdesk chatbot handled roughly 62% of queries in October without escalation, and People Ops is reviewing the top ten unanswered questions it logged to decide which ones should be added to the knowledge base. Two of those questions concerned the timing of recall refunds, so the policy owner has been asked to confirm the current Friday batching rule before the next content update. The audit team also noted that chatbot transcripts are retained for 30 days, which satisfies the retention requirement flagged in SA-11. Overall the review found no access-control issues with the automated tool itself.
